ms.promise:
Create the initial deployment infrastructure and configuration for a simplified launch to achieve the following:
・setup and configure services to up and running base to each other
・cardano node
・cardano db-sync
・cardano-submit-api
・postgres
・blockfrost
・build working containers
・extract and adjust parameters from existing docker and kubernetes files
・add missing properties and fix some of existing
・create missing configs
・parameterize containers and create compose file
・extract common properties to evn values
・unify way how the parameters are passed
・define containers dependencies and connections
・adjust running scripts and os level commands
・kubernetes config
・translate working docker compose to kuberneters config
・add missing configs like networks, deployments or storages
・helm charts
・build charts config base of docker compose and kubernetes config
ms.criteria: The deployment infrastructure that we open-source reliably launches blockfrost and the associated services (cardano-submit-api, postgres) with production configurations.

ms.promise: The outputs will be a number of commitments to the GitHub repository which add improvements to the reliability and performance of the instances. These commits will illustrate the attempts we make to improve reliability and performance.
ms.criteria: The modifications should result in a demonstrable, quantifiable improvement to the performance of the deployment. As of now, the exact changes we will make are unknown. During this milestone we will tinker with the deployment configuration, and try to see what changes if any result in improving performance / reliability.

ms.promise: We will conduct a survey with developers and users of the tool to collect their feedback. The output will be a compilation of the feedback we obtained as-well-as our plans to address and concerns raised by users.
ms.criteria: The intended outcome is to collect user feedback so that we can see what types of improvements users want to see and what pain points they have when interacting with the current deployment so we can address them. The acceptance criteria is a compilation of useful actionable feedback. We will make a best effort attempt to get 5 responses from developers who actually used the deployment.
